newsitem.title: PERU: LIMA STOCKS END LOWER ON INVESTOR DISINTEREST.
newsitem.headline: LIMA STOCKS END LOWER ON INVESTOR DISINTEREST.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange made small overall losses Wednesday for the second consecutive session, as investors continued to ignore the market despite low-priced stocks, brokers said.
They did not expect that tendency to change Thursday.
According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index fell 0.81 percent to 2,038.55 points, while the blue- chip Selective Index fell 0.55 percent to 2,939.74.
"There are really cheap shares which no one is buying. What stopped us sleeping was the good trade in miner Volcan," said Carlos Ugaz, of Finvest brokerage.

Volcan, buoyed by the recent purchase of state mining company Centromin's Mahr Tunel unit which turned it into the country's leading zinc producer, saw its common and labor shares rise 10 percent and 6.3 percent to 29.70 soles and 27.00 soles respectively.

"This company has a high roof. It is in a process of increasing its capital to carry out its growth. Furthermore, it won an operating unit. It does not have to wait to produce a mineral which is at its best price," added Luis Cueva, of Argos brokerage.
The market's total trading volume was 44 million soles ($16.7 million) on 1,182 trades.

Despite Volcan's gains, fellow miner Morococha dipped 2.29 percent to 6.41 soles, while UPC Backus brewery group was off 0.84 percent to 2.36 soles, and benchmark Telefonica del Peru lost 0.47 percent to 6.37 percent.
